beliefs.practice: Read the cluster connection string only from the environment variable DOCUMENTDB_URI at runtime and never commit actual credentials or the URI to source control or logs; provide a .env.example with a placeholder instead.
Create a single, long-lived MongoDB client instance per process (reuse it across requests) and configure connection pooling (maxPoolSize/minPoolSize) rather than opening a new connection per request.
Require TLS/SSL for all connections (tls=true/tlsAllowInvalidCertificates=false in the URI or driver TLS options) and validate server certificates to prevent MITM.

Store and rotate database credentials in a secrets manager (e.g., Azure Key Vault) rather than in environment variables or files when possible; restrict database network access via firewall rules or VNet service endpoints.

Set an appropriate readPreference and writeConcern for the workload (e.g., readPreference=primaryPreferred or nearest; writeConcern=w or w=majority depending on consistency needs) and include those settings in the client URI or driver options.
Implement retry logic with exponential backoff for transient network errors and throttling responses (handle 429 and transient socket errors), and enable driver retryableWrites if supported.
Create indexes on all fields used in filters and sorts for core queries (e.g., customer_id, action_type, channel, timestamp) and avoid collection scans for propensity and channel lookups.

For vector search, create a vector index (DiskANN/HNSW/IVF as provided by the cluster) on the embedding field, store embeddings as a consistent vector type/shape, and ensure the index parameters (metric, dimension) match stored vectors.

Keep embedding vectors and large binary fields in a dedicated collection (or dedicated field with careful size limits) rather than embedding large vectors in frequently-updated core customer documents to reduce document size and update cost.

Choose a partition/ shard key that evenly distributes load (e.g., customer_id) and ensure queries include the partition key when possible to take advantage of partition routing and avoid hot partitions.
Use TTL indexes for ephemeral data (e.g., demo NBA recommendations or temporary logs) to automatically expire old documents and avoid manual cleanup.

When seeding test/demo data, write only to the specified database sample_customer_360_03 and to namespaced collections (e.g., sample_customer_360_03.nba_recommendations or test_ prefixes) and ensure seed scripts can be run idempotently and cleaned up.

Use upsert operations (findOneAndUpdate with upsert:true or updateOne with upsert) for writing recommendations to avoid duplicate documents and include created_at/updated_at and agent provenance metadata in the document.
Use projection to fetch only required fields (e.g., history timestamps and action types or embeddings) when evaluating propensity/channel/timing agents to reduce bandwidth and latency.
Use explain() / query plans to validate that your core queries are using indexes; if sorts are necessary, create compound indexes that match the sort order (e.g., {customer_id:1, timestamp:-1}).
Page result sets using limit and a stable sort key (e.g., timestamp desc + _id) rather than skip for large offsets to maintain performance and avoid scanning skipped documents.
Detect and handle server-side throttling by watching for quota or RU/ops metrics and handle 429 responses with the Retry-After header and exponential backoff; monitor cluster metrics and set alerts.

Validate and enforce document schema at the application layer or via DB validators (shape, required fields, vector dimension) so the propensity/channel/timing agents receive consistent inputs and embeddings of fixed dimensionality.

Avoid large multi-document transactions when possible; if transactions are required, keep them short and, where supported, limit them to a single partition key to reduce cross-partition coordination cost.

Tune vector index ANN parameters (e.g., efSearch/efConstruction or DiskANN/HNSW params) for the recall/latency tradeoff you need, and persist those index parameters as part of infra-as-code so builds create identical indexes.

Store recommendation audits and agent inputs/outputs (propensity score, chosen channel, send time, feature snapshot) alongside the stored NBA document for traceability and offline analysis, but respect PII minimization.
Protect against injection-style misuse of query operators by sanitizing user-supplied filters and disallowing raw pipeline/$where inputs from untrusted sources.

In CI/tests, distinguish unit tests (mock DB) from integration tests (live cluster); skip or gate live-cluster tests unless DOCUMENTDB_URI is provided and tests are explicitly allowed to modify the sample_customer_360_03 database.

When creating indexes programmatically, verify that the cluster supports the requested index type (e.g., cosmosSearch/vector-diskann) and fall back to documented manual/CLI steps or include clear instructions in README if programmatic creation fails.

Instrument and log key performance indicators (latency, QPS, 4xx/5xx, 429s) and correlate them with deployment changes; capture and monitor slow queries to guide index additions and schema adjustments.
